summary: Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Rumtek Monastery and Young Lamas Home School under numerous traditional teachers. He founded the Rangjung Yeshe Institute in 1981 and became abbot of Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling in 1976.
Chong Go is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Dongguk University and under traditional teacher Daehaeng (attested 2012).
Chris Clark specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Sydney by 2015 under Mark Allon, where he was attested as an honorary associate in 2019.
Chris Williams specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He was attested in 2026 as an MPhil and PhD student and teaching staff member at the University of Bristol, supervised by Rita Langer.

Christian August Brandis was a philosopher and historian who studied at Kiel University (~1808–1812). He held academic posts at the University of Copenhagen (~1812–1815), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1815–1821), and the University of Bonn (~1821–1867).

Christian Bartholomae worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics, having studied under Heinrich Hübschmann. He held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1879–1885), Münster (~1885–1898), Giessen (~1898–1901), and Heidelberg University (~1909–1924).

Christian Bernert specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the International Buddhist Academy and the University of Vienna, earning a Mag. phil. under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, with additional instruction from Junjie Chu, Karin Preisendanz, and Gerald Hödl.

Christian Charles Josias von Bunsen was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and history. He studied at Marburg, Göttingen, Leiden, Copenhagen, and Munich, learning under Christian Gottlob Heyne and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, and founded the German Archaeological Institute in 1829.

Christian Coseru specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned degrees at the University of Bucharest and the Australian National University, and held posts including Associate Professor at the College of Charleston and Numata Visiting Professor at UC Berkeley (~2022).

Christian Gottlob Heyne worked in linguistics and history. After completing his master's degree at Leipzig University (1748–1752), he served at the University of Göttingen as Professor der Beredsamkeit und Dichtkunst (1763) and as director of its library (1764–1812).

Christian K. Wedemeyer works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Wesleyan and Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman, he held positions at Antioch, Columbia, the University of Copenhagen (2000–2003), and the University of Chicago (2003–2011).

Christian Lassen was an Indologist and linguist who studied under August Wilhelm von Schlegel at the University of Bonn. He spent his career at Bonn, serving as Privatdozent in 1830 and as professor of Old Indian language and literature from 1840 to 1876.

Christian Lee Novetzke specializes in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Macalester College, Harvard, and Columbia University, he taught at the University of Pennsylvania (2003–2007) and became Director of the South Asia Center at the University of Washington in 2007.
Christian Lindtner was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his doctorate at the University of Copenhagen by 1982 and served there as a professor (attested 1980–1991).

Christian Luczanits works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and art history/archaeology. He earned his master's and PhD at the University of Vienna and has held posts as a visiting professor at Stanford and UC Berkeley, and as a curator at the Rubin Museum of Art.

Christian Matthias Boehm specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London (attested 2005) under the supervision of John T. Carpenter, and also studied under Toshifumi Konno.

Christian Parker Bardolph Haskett specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2010), having also studied under Robert A. F. Thurman, and held an affiliation at Washington and Lee University (attested 2010).

Christian Wittern works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and computational humanities, having studied under Seizan Yanagida. He held posts at Hanazono University (attested 2011) and Kyoto University, where he was attested as professor in 1993 and affiliated in 2008.

Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Leiden University (~1884–1888). He served as an assistant professor at the University of Amsterdam (1892–1899) and as a professor at Leiden University (1899–1926).
Christine Chojnacki is an Indologist who completed her doctoral thesis at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1991. She served as a professor at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 (attested 2018).
